# TomTom AI marketplace skills for the feature-refinement track

For the speaker preparing the **"Refining features with Claude"** track. Loop: **Pick → Research → Plan → Build → Verify → Share**.

This catalog reviews both marketplace repos (`ai-coding-agent-marketplace`, `guidance-ai-tools`) plus all open PRs. Skill/plugin "twins" are collapsed to one row each (the plugin is just the installable wrapper for the same skill). The "Available now" table is filtered to **relevance score ≥ 3**; the ~50 score-1/2 domain tools are swept into "Not relevant / skip" so the signal isn't buried.

---

The handful most worth demoing live. Chosen to **span the whole loop**, not cluster on one phase.

| Pick | Why | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **design-doc** (`/design-doc:write`) | Turns a picked feature into a researched, template-conformant TomTom RFC/tech-design and publishes to Confluence — your Research+Plan engine. Score 5. | `ai-coding-agent-marketplace` · `catalog/design-doc/commands/write.md` |
| **jira-ticket-writer** | Structures a rough idea into a Why/How/To-Do/Definition-of-Done ticket and files it in Jira. Product-agnostic; anchors the Pick/Plan stage. Score 5. | `ai-coding-agent-marketplace` · `catalog/jira-ticket-writer/skills/jira-ticket-writer/SKILL.md` |
| **multi-agent-code-review** | Parallel specialist agents (correctness, design, security, perf) review the feature diff and synthesise one prioritised report. The core Verify tool. Score 5. | `ai-coding-agent-marketplace` · `catalog/multi-agent-code-review/skills/multi-agent-code-review/SKILL.md` |
| **wip** (+ wip-save) | Checkpoints plan + progress so a multi-session refinement loop survives across sessions. Spans the whole loop. Score 4. | `guidance-ai-tools` · `plugins/wip/skills/wip/SKILL.md` |
| **extract-ai-feedback** | Auto-captures how the AI performed straight from the session transcript — doubly on-theme for an event about evaluating AI tooling. Share stage. Score 4. | `guidance-ai-tools` · `plugins/experimental-skills/skills/extract-ai-feedback/SKILL.md` |

Coverage check: Pick (jira-ticket-writer) → Research/Plan (design-doc) → Build/cross-session (wip) → Verify (multi-agent-code-review, make-pr-green) → Share (extract-ai-feedback). Pick→Share is covered; **Build has no domain-agnostic driver** (see Gaps).

## Gaps (be honest)

- **Build is the weakest-covered phase.** There is **no domain-agnostic skill that drives the actual code-build** of an arbitrary backlog feature. The only end-to-end Build loops — `orbis-platform-jira-ticket` and the gosdk `bugfixer` — are domain-locked (Orbis platform / GO SDK Android). For a generic feature, Build relies on plain Claude Code plus enablers (signing, env vars). Set speaker expectations accordingly.
- **The catalog is overwhelmingly map-domain.** Roughly 50 of ~90 entries are score-1 map/data tooling (Orbis, NDS, Genesis, ODP, CoreDB, gosdk internals, sales/product agents). Only ~10 catalog skills are general enough for an arbitrary backlog feature; the rest pay off **only** if the picked feature happens to live in that domain.
- **The highest-relevance PRs are not merge-ready.** The two standout open PRs — make-pr-green (#24) and jira-tooling (#18) — are a DRAFT and a v0.1.0 respectively, and both need Atlassian/`gh` credentials or a sibling plugin installed. Demo them, but don't promise them as turnkey.
- **Credential/MCP dependencies are pervasive** in the otherwise-relevant tools: jira-ticket-writer and jira-tree need the Atlassian MCP; map/simulation tools need Databricks tokens or Orbis API keys (and VPN). Have these wired up before the session or the live demo stalls.

## Not relevant / skip (reviewed and dismissed)

Everything below scored 1–2 and was set aside for a general feature-refinement track:

- **Orbis / NDS / Genesis / ODP / MCR / CoreDB / Iris / RMS map-data skills** (orbis-specs, orbis-mcr, orbis-adp, orbis-odp-*, orbis-cc-rules, orbis-mcr, coredb, dumbo, genesis-rms/specs, iris, nds-viewer/-knowledge/-live/-planning/-portal/-stats, simple-ai-nds-database-inspector, map-test-data, osc-analyzer, orbis-lane-model-basemap) — domain-specific data access/lookup; irrelevant unless the feature targets that exact data.
- **gosdk-dev internals & app-user agents** (ttp/route/gpx conversion, install-*-apk, logcat, mapcat, lln-knowledge, call-routing-api, nav-demo-app-debug-*, ana/oneapp/nav-demo app-users) — GO SDK/Android-nav specific. (The bundling plugin itself is listed at score 3 above for that domain.)
- **Business-analytics agents** (product-agent, sales-agent, mixpanel-analytics) — Salesforce/PGT/PPDA data Q&A, out of scope for an engineering feature.
- **Narrow Verify/security niches** (jvm-diagnostics, fix-code-vulnerabilities, pwsh-script-security-check, sentry, k8s-devtest-deploy) — only fire for one specific tech stack or pre-existing findings, not the new feature diff.
- **Repo-onboarding / CI chores** (orbis-platform-onboard-sonarqube, apps-development-onboarding, babysit-dependabot-prs, orbis-platform-validate-git-operations, sensitive-file-guard) — one-time setup or guardrails, tangential to refining one feature.
- **Workflow/cosmetic** (voice-coordinator, caveman, tomtom-tov, wip-setup, wip-hud-setup) — novelty, brand-copy, or one-time config; not a loop driver.
- **Skill-authoring meta-tools** (skill-quality-review, sync-skills, create-plugin's review siblings) — only relevant if the picked feature *is itself* a Claude skill; this track builds product features. (plugin-creator kept at 4 for the Share-stage packaging case.)
- **Repo-local maintainer skills** (marketplace-build-pipeline, marketplace-ci-governance, semgrep-ai-ruleset) — not shipped via any plugin; internal marketplace tooling.
- **Skip-level open PRs**: #84, #48 (orbis-mcr/adp doc refinements to already-narrow skills), #69 (reliable-deck-builder — deck building, not code; useful only as a Verify-pattern reference), #21 (sync-agents — config plumbing), #19 (team-onboarding — pre-loop env setup, localization-specific), #17 (mine-pr-case-studies — retrospective analysis, needs a PR corpus the event won't have), #13 (splitting-big-prs refactor — no new attendee-visible capability).
